question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Play for time

options.text: To do something in the stipulated time
To make excuses or do things to gain time
To play something for the sake of old times
To play music in the time provided

solution:
The correct answer is "**to make excuses or do things to gain time**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that has a particular meaning** that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

 
 
• **For example**: Rain cats and dogs: to rain very heavily.

 
 
• The sky suddenly turned gray and it rained cats and dogs for almost an hour.
 
 
 
 
 
• The **given idiom "play for time" means to make excuses and delay until you are ready**.
 
 
• **Example**: My computer crashed just as the meeting began, so I had to play for time while I waited for it to reboot.
 
 
 
• From the given explanation it is clear that the meaning of the given idiom is "To make excuses or do things to gain time".
 
• Hence, the **correct answer is option 2)**.
